name: Pearson product-moment correlation
variables: n matched observations of x and y; r sample linear correlation in [−1,1]
assumptions: Comparable aligned observations and positive centered sums of squares; classical inferential reference needs independent pairs and bivariate normality.
limitations: Zero linear correlation does not establish independence; sensitive to outliers and nonlinear association.
computation: Center paired variables and divide the cross-product by the product of their Euclidean norms.

source.citation: SciPy pearsonr API, definition and assumptions. https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.pearsonr.html

name: Empirical discrete mutual information
definition: I(X;Y)=Σ_(i,j:p_ij>0) p_ij ln[p_ij/(p_i·p_j)], using empirical joint and marginal category frequencies.
variables: p_ij empirical joint proportions; p_i,p_j marginal proportions; I information in nats
assumptions: Aligned finite categorical observations and nonempty sample; positive joint cells have positive marginals; categories defined consistently.
limitations: Finite-sample upward bias, especially with sparse cells; no causal or inferential conclusion from the descriptive value alone.
failure_conditions: Misaligned pairs or outcome-dependent category selection
computation: Construct a contingency table, compute proportions, and sum contributions from positive joint cells.
application: Describe categorical dependence in authorised development data.
required_inputs: Aligned categorical pairs and prespecified category definitions.
incompatible_methods: Treating plug-in information as an unbiased population estimate
mechanism_note: KL divergence of the joint distribution from its product of marginals; a specific dependence functional, not a new independent source of evidence.

name: Cramér V categorical association
definition: V=√[X²/(N·min(r−1,c−1))], where X² is the uncorrected Pearson contingency statistic.
variables: N sample size; r,c numbers of categories; X² Pearson statistic; V∈[0,1]
assumptions: Valid nonempty contingency table with at least two positive-margin categories on each axis.
limitations: Unsigned descriptive association, potentially upward biased in sparse tables; not an independent significance test.
failure_conditions: Zero marginal category totals or invalid observations
computation: Calculate uncorrected Pearson chi-square and normalize by sample size and the smaller category dimension.
application: Summarize categorical association magnitude on aligned development observations.
required_inputs: Authorised contingency counts from comparable categories.
incompatible_methods: Counting the effect size and its underlying chi-square as independent findings
mechanism_note: Deterministic normalization of Pearson X² given dimensions and sample size; descriptive effect size only.

name: Double-centred sample distance correlation
definition: For paired vectors define A_ij=a_ij−mean_row_i(a)−mean_col_j(a)+mean(a), a_ij=||x_i−x_j||₂, and B similarly for y. V²_xy=n^(−2)Σ_ij A_ij B_ij; R²=V²_xy/√(V²_xx V²_yy) when denominator>0, otherwise 0.
variables: n paired vectors; A,B doubly centered Euclidean distance matrices; V²_xy empirical squared distance covariance; R² empirical squared distance correlation
assumptions: Aligned finite observations; population interpretation needs finite first moments and suitable independent sampling; stated version is biased empirical statistic.
limitations: Quadratic naive memory and time cost; finite sample dependence estimate not a standalone significance test; sensitive to feature scaling.
failure_conditions: Invalid pair alignment or incomparable feature units
computation: Compute pairwise Euclidean distances and double-center; calculate normalized matrix inner products, handling zero denominator explicitly.

source.citation: dcor theory documentation and Székely, Rizzo and Bakirov (2007). https://dcor.readthedocs.io/en/latest/theory.html

application: Assess nonlinear dependence among aligned historical measurements on authorised development records.
